previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of recurrent pulmonary emboli, chronic pain, COPD, and anticoagulation on Lovenox was admitted for worsening bilateral pleuritic chest pain and new right bicep pain. He was concerned about a new clot but showed no clinical signs of acute cardiopulmonary deterioration. A chest X-ray revealed no acute process, and a right upper extremity ultrasound showed no DVT. Pain was managed with a short-term increase in oxycodone from 5mg to 10mg every 4 hours, with plans to taper back to baseline. Anxiety was addressed with hydroxyzine and non-pharmacologic strategies. His condition stabilized, pain improved, and he was discharged home with instructions to continue Lovenox, taper oxycodone over 8 days, and follow up with pain management. No new clots were diagnosed during this admission.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

It was a pleasure taking care of you at ___ 
___. You were admitted for diarrhea, abdominal pain, 
and chest pain. Your chest pain was likely a result of the 
chronic muscle or bone inflammation you have experienced in the 
past. 
We do not think your chest pain was caused by your heart, as 
your cardiac enzymes were normal and a test looking at the 
electricity of your heart (EKG) was normal. 

Your abdominal pain was similar to your chronic abdominal pain 
and may have been worse with your recent soft stools. Your 
diarrhea may have been caused by an infection, most likey a 
virus. It resolved during your stay when you began to produce 
more well-formed stools.

It was also discovered using imaging techniques that you had a 
new blood clot in a large vein that runs through your body. The 
filter you have had for ___ years did its job and caught the clot 
before it could cause damage or lung problems. This clot was 
most likely caused by the interruption for 5 days in your 
lovenox anticoagulation therapy.  You were seen by vascular 
surgery here and they recommended that you continue on your home 
lovenox; they did not recommend any surgical intervention for 
your IVC filter.

It is critically important that you take your lovenox everyday 
or you could die from complications from blood clots. We are 
sending a prescription to the ___ pharmacy you requested in 
___. You will be discharged on several days of pain 
medications for your chronic pain. It is important that you 
followup with a primary care physician and ___ pain clinic to 
manage your chronic pain.

We must reiterate that you should followup with a primary care 
physician within days to manage your lovenox. We suggested that 
you continue care with your primary care physician at ___, 
Dr. ___ you no longer wished to continue care there. We 
have, however, spoken with Dr. ___ left a message so that 
he has all the necessary information. We also tried to establish 
care here with Dr. ___ you did not desire this option. 
Because of your prior narcotics violations within our system, we 
are unable at this time to set you up with another primary care 
physician ___.

We will prescribe a month's course of lovenox. In the meanwhile, 
you should contact your insurance company and request a list of

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with history of multiple thromboses presenting
with abdominal pain and chest pain, off anticoagulations for five days.  Rule
out pulmonary embolism or arterial thrombus.

COMPARISONS:  Multiple prior CTs, most recently CT chest ___ and
CT abdomen and pelvis of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT images were obtained from the thoracic inlet to the upper
abdomen after administration of 120 cc of IV Omnipaque contrast timed for
opacification of the thoracic aorta.  Images were subsequently acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis.  An additional arterial phase sequence was
obtained through the abdominal aorta after administration of additional IV
contrast.

FINDINGS:

CHEST CTA:  The great vessels are normal caliber.  The thoracic aorta is
normal without aneurysm or dissection.  The main, lobar, segmental, and
proximal subsegmental pulmonary arteries are opacified without filling defect.
The previously identified pulmonary emboli are no longer visualized.

CHEST:  

No axillary, mediastinal, or hilar lymphadenopathy.  The heart is normal size.
No pericardial effusion.  4-mm right lower lobe nodule is similar to ___ but minimally enlarged since ___.  No focal consolidation,
pleural effusion, pneumothorax, or pneumomediastinum.  Airways are patent to
subsegmental levels.  The esophagus is normal.  

ABDOMEN:

The liver, gallbladder, intra- and extra-hepatic bile ducts, pancreas, and
adrenal glands are normal.  The spleen is absent.  A 1.3-cm splenule is noted.
A 2.0-cm cystic lesion in the lower pole of the left kidney is of intermediate
density, and is enlarged since ___, previously partially
characterized on ultrasound as a complex cyst.  Cortical defects of the right
kidney are similar to prior.  The kidneys enhance symmetrically and excrete
contrast promptly.  The ureters are normal in course and caliber.

The stomach is normal.  The small and large bowel have a normal course and
caliber.

The abdominal aorta is unremarkable without aneurysm or dissection.  No
filling defect is present within the abdominal aorta.  The celiac axis has
conventional anatomy.  The splenic artery is not opacified.  The portal veins
are patent.

An infrarenal IVC filter appears in similar position to prior, but one of the
prongs of the IVC filter is now oriented superiorly and abuts the IVC wall. 
No active extravasation of contrast or large adjacent hematoma.  A
non-obstructing thrombus extends from the superior aspect of the IVC filter
and appears new since ___.

No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  No free abdominal fluid or
pneumoperitoneum.  The patient is status post ventral hernia repair.  A right
fat-containing Spigelian hernia (2B:98) is similar to prior.

The bladder and terminal ureters are normal.  The prostate gland and seminal
vesicles are normal.  No pelvic sidewall or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  No free
pelvic fluid.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  No focal lytic or sclerotic lesion concerning for
malignancy.  Multilevel thoracolumbar spine degenerative changes are present.

IMPRESSION:  

1.  New non-occlusive IVC thrombus extending superiorly from the infrarenal
IVC filter.  A prong of the IVC filter is newly oriented superiorly and abuts
the wall of the IVC.  No active extravasation of contrast or adjacent
hematoma.

2.  No pulmonary embolus visualized.  Previously seen pulmonary emboli no
longer present.

3.  2.0 cm intermediate density left lower pole renal cyst, previously
characterized on US as a complex cyst, has enlarged since ___.  Given
complexity and continued enlargement, MR is recommended for further
evaluation.

4.  4-mm right lower lobe pulmonary nodule, stable since ___, but
increased since ___.  Follow-up suggested in 6 months.

5.  Right fat-containing Spigelian hernia, similar to prior.

Findings were discussed in person by ___ with ___ on ___ at 1154 A.M.
